do: Block the wheels that stay on the ground
Front: jack at the centre of the crossmember
caution: Use only the specified jacking positions (p.G-2).

do: Front: set a safety stand under each side of the body frame and lower onto them
caution: The car is supported on safety stands, not on the jack (p.G-2).

do: Rear: jack at the differential
Rear: set a safety stand under each side of the body frame and lower onto them
Clear the engine bay of tools and people before starting the engine
Release the parking brake, put the selector in neutral and set the key to ACC
caution: Brake assist does not work with the engine off.

do: Tow with the rear wheels off the ground: raised, or on dollies
how: SP-1542. The rear wheels are the drive wheels.
caution: Never tow backward with the drive wheels on the ground.

do: If all four wheels must stay on the ground, tow forward only, slowly and for a short distance
how: The 1985 manual's limit is SP-1543 (another gearbox); no figure for this car's 3N71B is in the record, so keep the rear wheels up whenever it can be done.

do: On a hook, pull straight away from it and take up the slack slowly
caution: The rear hook is for emergency recovery only.

do: Warm the engine if it is cold
Take off the oil filler cap and drain the oil
how: The cap off lets the oil drain easily.

do: Fit the new filter
how: SP-1546: oil the gasket, fully hand tight, then 1/8 turn more with a band-type wrench.
caution: Never a chain-type filter wrench.

do: Fill with oil to the F mark on the dipstick
how: Grade SP-023, viscosity SP-775, capacity SP-144.

do: Start the engine, check for leaks, then recheck the level
how: Look at the filter joint and the drain plug washer; top up if needed.
expect: No leak at either; level at F.

do: Check each belt for cracks or other damage
Press each belt with the thumb and measure its deflection; adjust if it is out
how: About 10 kg (22 lb) of thumb pressure. Alternator belt SP-025; air pump belt SP-761; A/C belt SP-1001 (1985 figure).

do: Check each plug for burned or eroded electrodes, fouling or cracked porcelain
caution: Do not pull on the plug cables to remove them.

do: Measure the electrode gap; replace the plug if it is out
Refit with a little anti-seize or molybdenum thread lubricant on the first few threads
Check every cooling hose, heater hoses included, for cracks or wear; replace any that show it
Pressurise the system with a radiator cap tester and look for leaks
caution: Never above 1.05 kg/cm2 (SP-1547). Steam and hot water escape when the cap comes off a hot radiator.

do: Drain the coolant by removing the radiator drain plug
caution: A hot engine scalds: let it cool first.

do: Fill with new coolant mixed for the coldest weather expected
how: Mixture SP-1548; capacity SP-050; antifreeze type SP-056.

do: Check the brake pedal for smooth operation
Check the pedal height; adjust by turning the stop switch, then tighten its lock nut
Check the pedal free play; adjust by turning the push rod, then tighten its lock nut
Check the fluid level is near the MAX line of the reservoir; top up to MAX
Pull the parking brake lever with 10 kg (22 lb) and count its stroke; adjust with the adjusting nut
Check the booster vacuum hoses, connectors and check valve for cracks, chafing and deterioration
Engine off, press the pedal several times; then hold it down and start the engine
expect: Pedal travel does not change with the engine off; the pedal sinks a little as the engine starts.

do: Make a simple dipstick from a wire
Put the dipstick into the oil filler hole of the steering gear
Pull it out and measure dimension L; add gear oil if the level is low
how: L is SP-1550; oil is SP-252.

do: Remove the hub and the inner and outer bearings
Clean the bearings in solvent and inspect them for damage
Repack with grease and fit a new oil seal
how: SP-1552 names the grease and the five places it goes.

do: Look over the rear axle for oil leaks; find and repair the cause of any
Remove the filler plug and check the oil reaches the bottom edge of the hole
expect: Oil level at the bottom edge of the filler hole.

do: Pull each belt out to be sure it moves smoothly
Check the webbing for scratches, tears or wear and the metal fittings for bends
caution: Do not take the buckle or the retractor apart.

do: Check the retractors work
Check the anchor bolts are tight
Check the brake lines, hoses and connections
how: Properly attached and connected; no leaks, cracks, chafing, abrasion or deterioration.

do: Disc brakes: check caliper operation and leaks, pad wear, and the condition and thickness of the disc
Drum brakes: check wheel cylinder operation and leaks, lining wear or damage, and the inner surface and inner diameter of the drum
Check steering wheel free play, steering operation, looseness of the gear housing and any oil leaking from it
Check the steering linkage, tie rod ends and arms
how: No excessive play at the tie rod ends, no damaged dust boots, no looseness or grease leaking at the tie rod ends.

do: Check the front suspension ball joints for damage, looseness and grease leakage
Tighten the seat mounting bolts and retighten any loose front and rear suspension nuts and bolts to their torque
how: The torques are in the suspension rows of specs. Wheel nuts: interval wheel_nuts.

do: Check the exhaust heat shields and the exhaust itself
how: Clearance between insulator and body and between insulator and exhaust; pipes, hangers and connections for severe corrosion, leaks or damage.

do: Set the parking brake and block the wheels
Turn off all accessories and remove the fuel filler cap
Warm the engine to normal operating temperature
Disconnect the tube at the idle compensator in the air cleaner and plug its end
Check the dash pot rod and the A/C throttle opener do not hold the throttle lever off the idle stop
Read the idle speed; set it with the throttle adjust screw if it is out
Warm the engine to normal operating temperature
Connect a tachometer
Disconnect the connector with the BY and GB wires
how: The figure on the page shows which one; the figure was not read.

do: Put a voltmeter on each terminal, GY and LgY: negative probe on the terminal, positive probe on battery positive
Start the engine, drop it quickly from 3000 rpm and watch both meters
expect: Current flows to both terminals at the same moment, at 1100 +/-50 rpm.

do: If they do not switch together, take the cap off the throttle sensor adjusting screw and turn it
how: It sets when voltmeter A (LgY) switches: screw in is earlier, screw out is later.

do: Refit the cap on the adjusting screw
Spray cleaner on the choke linkage to remove dirt and grease
Spray cleaner on both ends of the choke shaft while moving the choke valve slowly by hand
Dry the sprayed areas with compressed air
Apply spray lubricant and work the choke lever several times
expect: The choke mechanism moves freely.

do: Turn the ignition on
expect: The oil level warning light comes on.

do: Start the engine
expect: The warning light goes off.

do: At idle, disconnect the connector from the oil level sensor and ground the terminal
expect: The warning light comes on and the chime sounds.

do: Remove the sensor and check the oil holes of its oil chamber are clear; clean them with solvent if not
Put an ohmmeter on the sensor and move the float up and down; replace the sensor if it reads otherwise
expect: Float up: no continuity. Float down: continuity.

do: Turn the ignition on
expect: The coolant level warning light comes on.

do: Start the engine
expect: The warning light goes off.

do: At idle, disconnect the connector from the level sensor
expect: The warning light comes on and the chime sounds.

do: Remove the radiator cap to release the pressure, then take the sensor out of the radiator and plug the hole
caution: Steam and hot water escape from a hot radiator.

do: Check the sensor for cracks or damage
Start the engine and ground the threaded part of the sensor; replace the sensor if the light stays off
expect: The coolant level warning light comes on.

do: Check the starting assist fluid level in the reservoir
Disconnect the connector from the magnet switch on the starter motor
Disconnect the connector from the oil thermo unit on the oil pan and ground the loose connector to the body
Hold the tank's air bleed button in and turn the key to START
expect: Starting assist fluid spouts from the nozzle.

do: Park on level ground and set the parking brake firmly
Idle the engine for about two minutes
Move the selector through every position and leave it in P
Read the dipstick
expect: Level between L and F.

do: Add fluid through the filler tube if it is low
caution: Do not overfill.

do: Warm the engine thoroughly and connect a tachometer
Connect a timing light to the plug lead of the front leading plug
Run the engine at its idle speed
Aim the light at the timing indicator pin on the front cover
expect: The yellow mark on the pulley sits at the pin.

do: If the leading timing is off, loosen the distributor lock nut, turn the distributor housing until it is right, tighten and recheck
Move the timing light to the lead of the front trailing plug and check the trailing timing
expect: The red mark on the pulley sits at the pin.

do: If the trailing timing is off, loosen the screws of the trailing vacuum unit, move the unit until it is right, tighten and recheck
Check the battery is fully charged
Warm the engine thoroughly, stop it and let it sit about ten minutes
how: The wait lets the catalytic converter cool. Conditions: SP-1559.

do: Remove the trailing plug of the rotor being measured and no other
caution: Never both trailing plugs out on a 12A: unburned mixture blows out of the plug holes.

do: Disconnect the primary wires of both the trailing and the leading coil
Connect the tester hose to the plug hole and its wires to the battery
how: A piston-engine tester will not do: SP-1559.

do: When the tester has warmed up, switch it on to feed the recording sheet
expect: A line 20-30 mm long is drawn to mark zero.

do: Hold the throttle wide open and crank the engine for 5 to 10 seconds
expect: The pressure of each chamber is plotted on the sheet.

do: Stop cranking and switch off the sheet feed
Measure the other rotor the same way
Judge the lowest pressure and the spread between the highest and the lowest
how: Limits SP-015 and SP-016. Cranking speed comes from the number of peaks plotted in 5 seconds; the graphs on p.1-12 correct for cranking speed and altitude.

do: Apply the parking brake and block the wheels
Drain the engine oil, then clean and refit the drain plug
Remove the engine under cover
Disconnect the battery negative cable and remove the hood
Disconnect the high-tension leads at the ignition coils
Disconnect the pick-up coil wiring connectors and the condenser lead
Disconnect the oil level sensor connector
Disconnect the water temperature gauge unit connector
Disconnect the oil pressure gauge unit connector
Disconnect the oil thermo sensor connector (not on California cars)
Disconnect the vacuum sensing tube of the transmission vacuum diaphragm (automatic) and the evaporative hose
Disconnect the coolant level sensor connector
Disconnect the coolant reservoir hose
Remove the air cleaner assembly
Disconnect the No. 2 water temperature switch connector
Drain the cooling system by taking the lower hose off the radiator
Disconnect the upper hose from the radiator
Disconnect the transmission oil pipes from the radiator (automatic only)
Remove the cooling fan and fan drive assembly
Remove the radiator and shroud assembly
Disconnect the power brake vacuum hose
Disconnect the air pipe from the rear end of the intake manifold
Disconnect the choke heater lead connectors
Disconnect the throttle sensor, idle richer solenoid and port air solenoid valve connectors, and the fourth the page lists
how: The OCR text garbles the name of the fourth valve.

do: Disconnect the accelerator cable, choke cable and hot start assist cable
Disconnect the cruise control cable if fitted
Disconnect the fuel main and return hoses
Disconnect the sub-zero start assist fluid hose (not on California cars)
Disconnect the connector and the battery lead at the rear of the alternator
Disconnect the No. 1 water temperature switch, air vent solenoid valve, vacuum switch, three way valve and the engine earth
Disconnect the water hoses
Unbolt the A/C compressor from the engine if fitted
Disconnect the wiring and remove the starter motor
Remove the bolts holding the transmission to the rear of the engine
Remove the exhaust pipe front cover
Loosen the nuts holding the exhaust pipe to the exhaust manifold
Support the monolith converter so it cannot drop
Support the front of the transmission with a jack
Remove the nuts from the right and left engine mountings
Fit a lifting sling to the engine hanger brackets, hook it to a hoist and take up the slack
Pull the engine forward until it is clear of the transmission, then lift it out
Fit hanger 49 1114 005 to engine stand 49 0107 680A and mount the engine on it
Remove the valve and piping assemblies from the engine
Installation is the reverse; then refill coolant and oil, tune the engine and check the hood closes properly
Air pump: disconnect the air outlet hose, remove the strap bolt, slip the belt off and remove the pump
Alternator: remove the strap bolt, slip the belt off and remove the alternator
Disconnect the connecting rod at the metering oil pump and the oil hoses at its outlets
Remove the exhaust manifold cover
Remove the intake manifold and carburettor assembly, then the gasket and O-rings
Remove the exhaust manifold, its gasket and the engine mount
Remove the distributor lock nut and the distributor
Remove the oil pipe, the water hose, the oil cooler with the oil filter, and the O-rings
caution: Leave the filter cartridge on the oil cooler unless it is being replaced.

do: Remove the A/C compressor pulley and the water pump
Remove the oil pan
caution: Do not damage the oil pan or the housings.

do: Remove the oil strainer and its gasket
Fit counter weight stopper 49 1881 055 to the counter weight, then remove the eccentric shaft pulley bolt and the pulley
Remove the front cover and gasket, and the O-ring on the oil passage
Slide the distributor drive gear off the shaft
Straighten the lock washer tab and remove the oil pump sprocket nut and lock washer
Slide both sprockets and the chain off the eccentric shaft and the oil pump shaft together
Remove the oil pump
Remove the key, balance weight, thrust washer and needle bearing
Remove the bearing housing, needle bearing, spacer and thrust plate
Fit the counter weight stopper to the rear housing and remove the drive plate
Remove the counter weight nut with box wrench 49 0820 035
Pull the counter weight with the puller, turning its handle and tapping its head lightly, then remove the key
caution: Do not drop the counter weight.

do: Loosen the tension bolts in the sequence of the figure, in two or three passes, and remove them
how: The 12A has no bolt No. 6 in the loosening sequence: skip it. The sequence figure was not read.
caution: Never loosen the bolts all at once.

do: Lift the rear housing off the shaft and put any seals stuck to it back in their places on the rotor

Rear rotor housing: remove the sealing rubbers and O-ring, pull the tubular dowels with puller 49 0813 215A while holding the housing down, lift the housing off, then remove the rubbers and O-ring from its front side
caution: Do not let the apex seals and side pieces drop off the rotor.

do: Put the side pieces, apex seals and springs of the rear rotor into seal case 49 0813 250 by the numbers beside each groove
Remove the corner seals with their soft seals, the corner seal springs, side seals and side seal springs into the seal case
Lift the rear rotor off and lay it internal gear down on a clean rubber pad or cloth
Remove the seals and springs of the other face into the seal case
With a protector over the inner oil seal lip, remove the outer oil seal with remover 49 0813 225, then the inner oil seal and the oil seal springs; repeat on the other face
caution: Never lever at one place only: the oil seal deforms.

do: Mark the rear rotor so it goes back in its own place
Pull the tubular dowels of the intermediate housing and remove it, sliding it past the rear rotor journal while holding it up and pushing the eccentric shaft up
Remove the eccentric shaft
caution: Do not damage the rotor bearing or the main bearing.

do: Remove the front rotor housing and the front rotor the same way as the rear
Side housings: remove the carbon with extra fine emery paper
caution: A carbon scraper must not mark the finished surfaces.

do: Side housings: remove the old sealing agent with a cloth or brush soaked in ketone or thinner
Rotor housing: before cleaning, look for traces of gas or water leakage along the inner margin of each side face
Rotor housing: wipe the carbon off the inner surface with a cloth, soaked in ketone or thinner if it is stubborn
Rotor housing: clear deposits and rust from the water passages, and wipe off the old sealing agent
Rotor: remove the carbon with carbon remover or emery paper, wash it in cleaning solution and blow it dry
caution: Do not damage the soft coating on the side surfaces of the rotor.

do: Seals and springs: remove all carbon and wash them in cleaning solution
caution: Never emery paper on the seals.

do: Side housings: check for warp with a straight edge
how: Limit SP-792; over it the housing is replaced.

do: Side housings: check the rotor sliding surface for stepped wear with a dial indicator on gauge body 49 0727 570
how: Limits SP-793, and SP-794 (the 1985 manual's finer figures).

do: Stationary gears: check for cracked, scored, worn or chipped teeth
Main bearings: check for wear, scratching and flaking, and work out the clearance from the bearing bore and the main journal diameter
Rotor housings: check the chromium plated surface for scoring and flaking
Rotor housings: measure the width with a micrometer at four points
Rotors: inspect for wear and damage, and the internal gear for cracked, scored, worn or chipped teeth
Rotors: work out the side housing to rotor clearance from the rotor housing width at point A and the largest of three rotor width readings
how: SP-839, limit SP-840 (the 1985 standard is SP-841). Too much: replace the rotor assembly. Too little: the internal gear has crept out - tap it back lightly with a plastic hammer and measure again.

do: Rotors: check the corner seal bores with the bore gauge
Rotor bearings: check for wear, flaking and scoring, and work out the clearance from the bearing bore and the rotor journal diameter
Rotor oil seals: check for wear, free movement in the groove under a finger, lip width and protrusion
how: SP-873 and SP-874; low protrusion means a new oil seal spring.

do: Apex seals and side pieces: check for wear and cracks, and measure the seal height at two positions
Apex seals: check warp as the gap between the top surfaces of two seals from the same rotor
how: SP-852; over it all three seals of that rotor are replaced.

do: Apex seals: measure the clearance to the rotor groove, the feeler gauge pushed to the bottom of the groove
Apex seal springs: check for wear and measure the free height
Side seals: check free movement, protrusion and the clearance to the groove
how: SP-864; SP-860, limit SP-861. Low protrusion means a new side seal spring.

do: Side seals: measure the clearance to the corner seal, both fitted on the rotor
how: SP-862, limit SP-863. A new side seal is fitted by filing one end to the round of the corner seal.

do: Corner seals, soft seals and springs: check for wear, cracks and heat damage, free movement and protrusion
how: SP-869; low protrusion means a new corner seal spring.

do: Eccentric shaft: check for cracks, scratches and wear and that the oil passages are open, then measure the run-out
how: Half the largest swing of the dial indicator. Limit SP-824.

do: Eccentric shaft: check the blind plug in the shaft end for leaks or looseness, and the oil jets for a weak spring or a sticking or damaged ball
how: A leaking plug comes out with a hexagon key for a new O-ring.

do: Check the needle bearing, bearing housing and thrust plate for wear or damage
Front and rear eccentric shaft oil seals: if worn, pull the seal, clean the bore and tap a new one home through a block of hardwood
caution: No lubricant or sealer on the outside of the seal; never the hammer directly on it.

do: Oil pump drive: check the chain for broken links and both sprockets for cracks and worn or damaged teeth
Front main bearing: remove the stationary gear and bearing with puller and installer 49 0813 235
Press the bearing out with the tool without its adaptor ring
With the adaptor ring fitted and the bearing lug in line with the slot of the gear, press the new bearing in until the adaptor touches the gear flange
Fit the stationary gear to the front housing, the slot of its flange on the dowel pin of the housing
Rear main bearing: remove the stationary gear bolts, pull the gear with the same tool and change the bearing as in steps 2 and 3
Rear: a new O-ring with a thin coat of vaseline in the gear groove, sealing agent on the gear flange, the gear onto the rear housing with its slot on the dowel pin, and the bolts tightened
caution: Do not damage the O-ring.

do: Rotor bearing: rotor on a support with the internal gear down, press the bearing out with tool 49 0813 240 without its adaptor ring
caution: Do not damage the internal gear.

do: Turn the rotor gear up, set the new bearing with its lug in line with the slot of the rotor bore, and press it in with the adaptor ring until it is flush with the rotor boss
Rotor on a clean rubber pad or cloth: fit the oil seal springs, the round end of each in the stopper hole of its groove
Fit a new O-ring in each oil seal, place the inner oil seal with the square edge of the spring in its stopper notch, and press it down with a used inner oil seal
caution: Do not deform the lip of the oil seal.

do: Fit the outer oil seal the same way, pressing slowly with the fingers, then do the other face of the rotor
expect: Each oil seal moves smoothly when pressed.

do: Front rotor, internal gear up: put the apex seals in their grooves without spring or side piece, the side-piece end toward the rear face of the rotor
Fit the soft seals into the corner seals, then corner seal springs and corner seals, side seal springs and side seals into their grooves
expect: Each seal moves smoothly when its head is pressed.

do: Put a rubber ring round the rotor so the apex seals cannot drop out
Mount the front housing on the stand and set the front rotor on it, the gears meshed with one apex at one of the four positions of the figure
caution: Do not drop a seal into the port.

do: Oil the front rotor journal and the main journal and insert the eccentric shaft
caution: Do not damage the rotor bearing or the main bearing.

do: Sealing agent on the front side of the front rotor housing, then a new O-ring and new sealing rubbers
Turn the rotor housing over onto the front housing without losing the rubbers, oil the tubular dowels and push them through into the front housing
Rear face of the rotor: apex seal springs with both ends under the back of the seal, corner seals, side seals, and each side piece in its original place with its spring seated
expect: Each seal moves smoothly when its head is pressed.

do: Sealing agent, new O-ring, sealing rubbers and protector on the rear side of the front rotor housing, then engine oil on the seals and the sliding surface
caution: No foreign matter in the rotor housing.

do: Lift the eccentric shaft a little and fit the intermediate housing over it
Fit the rear rotor and the rear rotor housing the same way as the front
Oil the stationary gear and main bearing well and fit the rear housing
Oil the tension bolt threads, fit the bolts and tighten them gradually in the sequence of the figure
how: Torque SP-161. The 12A has no bolt No. 11 in the tightening sequence: skip it. New sealing washers at an overhaul. The sequence figure was not read.
expect: The eccentric shaft turns lightly and smoothly.

do: Oil the oil seal in the rear housing, fit the key and the counter weight, put sealing agent on the lock nut face, hold with stopper 49 1881 055 and tighten the nut with box wrench 49 0820 035
Fit the drive plate with its hole and the counter weight placed as the figure shows
Slide the thrust plate (chamfer down), spacer and needle bearing onto the shaft and oil them, then fit the bearing housing to the front housing and tighten its bolts
Slide on the second needle bearing, oiled, then the balance weight with the thrust washer
Fit the oil pump to the front housing and the key to its shaft, put the chain on both sprockets and slide them on together with key and keyway in line
Line up the keyways of the shaft sprocket and the balance weight and fit the key, then slide on the distributor drive gear with its F mark to the front
Fit the pulley and tighten its bolt, then measure the eccentric shaft end play with a dial indicator on the rear housing against the counter weight
how: Bolt SP-160. End play SP-825, limit SP-826; corrected with a thicker or thinner spacer, SP-829.

do: Take the pulley off, tighten the oil pump sprocket nut and bend the lock washer tab, then check the chain slack with a finger
New O-ring on the oil passage, gasket and front cover on and bolted, oil on the front cover seal, then the pulley with a new washer under its bolt
Fit the oil strainer and gasket, trim the gaskets flush with the pan face, clean the faces, lay the sealer bead on the oil pan and tighten its bolts little by little in turn
Put two O-rings on the oil filter body, fit the filter body and oil cooler and connect the water hose
caution: Never take the oil cooler apart from its body: it will leak oil.

do: Set the leading (yellow) mark of the pulley at the indicator pin, line up the tally marks of the distributor housing and driven gear, and fit the distributor and lock nut
Turn the distributor housing until the projection of the signal rotor lines up with the core of the leading pick-up coil, tighten the lock nut and fit the rotor and cap
Fit the engine mount, then the gasket and the exhaust manifold
Place the O-rings and gasket and fit the intake manifold and carburettor assembly, in the reverse order of removal
Fit the alternator to its bracket, then the belt, and set the belt tension
Fit the air pump and its belt and set the belt tension
With the engine off the stand, fit the oil cooler oil pipe with its sealing washers, both ends partly tightened, then tighten the front cover nut and after it the cooler bolt
caution: The cooler-side bolt first leaves the front cover joint leaking.

do: Disconnect the connector from the oil pressure gauge unit on the rear housing
Remove the gauge unit and screw oil pressure gauge 49 0187 280 into its hole
Start the engine and warm it to normal operating temperature
Read the pressure at idle (in D) and at 3000 rpm
how: Idle SP-019 (the 1985 manual gives SP-1566); 3000 rpm SP-020.
expect: Both readings inside their ranges.

do: If a reading is out, check the oil level is between F and L, then the pressure regulator and the pressure control valve, then the oil pump
how: Control valve: PR-038. Oil pump: PR-037.

do: Remove the water hoses from the inlet and outlet sides of the cooler
Remove the oil pipe and its sealing washer
Remove the oil cooler and the oil filter cartridge together as one unit, then the O-rings
how: The cooler is replaced as an assembly.

do: Fit in the reverse order with a new filter cartridge, new O-rings and a new sealing washer
Add engine oil and coolant
Start the engine and check for oil and water leaks
expect: No leak at the cooler or the pipe.

do: Check the metering oil pump and its hoses for leaks and the lever to washer clearance
Connect a tachometer and warm the engine to normal operating temperature
Disconnect the two metering oil hoses at the carburettor
Hold the engine at 2000 rpm with the two hoses in a measuring cylinder
caution: Add clean engine oil into the carburettor while measuring: the engine is getting none.

do: Stop the engine after 6 minutes and read the amount of oil
how: SP-1569; out of range the pump is replaced.

do: Drain the engine oil and remove the engine under cover
Disconnect the oil level sensor connector
Disconnect the connector of the oil thermo unit (not on California cars)
Remove the oil pan
Check the oil pan for cracks and damaged drain plug threads and straighten its mating face if it needs it
Clean the mating faces of the housings and the oil pan
Lay a continuous, overlapped bead of sealer on the mounting face of the oil pan; with a silicone sealer use the gasket too, sealer on both of its sides
Fit the oil pan and tighten its bolts little by little in turn
Remove the oil pump from the front housing
Take it apart in order: snap ring, rear outer rotor, rear inner rotor, key, screw, middle plate, front outer rotor, front inner rotor, key, shaft
Measure the clearance between the lobes of the rotors with a feeler gauge
how: SP-885, limit SP-886; over the limit both rotors are replaced.

do: Measure the clearance between the outer rotor and the pump body
how: SP-887, limit SP-888; over the limit the rotor or the body is replaced.

do: Measure the end float of the rotors: a straight edge across the pump body for the gap to the rotor, then across the mating face of the front housing for the gap to the housing
how: SP-889, limit SP-890; over the limit the pump body is ground.

do: Fit the front inner rotor with the shaft and the front outer rotor into the pump body
Fit the middle plate, then the set screw in line with the recess of the plate, and caulk the screw
Fit the rear inner and outer rotors, marks the same way, and the snap ring on the shaft
Prime the pump with engine oil, bolt it to the front housing and turn the shaft by hand
expect: The shaft turns smoothly.

do: Check the oil pressure once the engine runs
Remove the pressure control valve from the front cover
Examine the spring and the plunger for corrosion or damage; replace them if it is severe
Measure the free length of the spring and replace the spring if it is out
Engine cold, turn the fan by hand
expect: Resistance is felt.

do: Check the fan drive clutch for fluid leaks, the bimetal for deformation and the bearing for play or grease leaks
To replace the clutch, remove the fan and fan drive assembly, undo the fan bolts and separate the fan from the drive
Assemble the fan to the new drive and refit in the reverse order
Drain the cooling system by disconnecting the radiator lower hose
Remove the air cleaner
Disconnect the radiator upper hose
Remove the thermostat cover and its gasket, and lift out the thermostat
Put the thermostat in water with a thermometer and heat the water gradually
Note the temperature at which it starts to open and at which it is fully open, and measure the lift fully open
how: Opening SP-748 and lift SP-749; the 1985 manual's figures are SP-051.

do: Fit the thermostat with its jiggle pin on the upper side
caution: Pin elsewhere, the opening temperature changes.

do: Fit the thermostat cover, connect the upper hose, refit the air cleaner and connect the lower hose
Fill the radiator with coolant
Put the radiator cap on a tester and raise the pressure gradually
expect: The cap holds within its range.

do: Wait about 10 seconds and see whether the pressure has dropped
how: SP-753. A cap that does not reach the bottom of the range or goes over the top is replaced.

do: Examine the radiator for leaks; any leak, however small, is soldered fully or the radiator replaced
Blow the outside of the core clean with compressed air and check the rubber gasket of the cap
how: A cap with a damaged gasket is replaced.

do: Take the cap off, add coolant if it is low and fit the cap tester to the radiator
caution: To take a cap off hot: SP-1575.

do: Warm the engine to normal operating temperature and stop it
Pump the system up and watch the gauge for about a minute
expect: The pressure holds.

do: If the pressure drops, look over every hose and fitting for an external leak
Disconnect the No. 2 water temperature switch connector and the coolant level sensor lead
Disconnect the water hose to the reservoir
Remove the cooling fan and fan drive assembly
Disconnect the radiator lower hose and drain the cooling system
Disconnect the heater hose and the radiator upper hose
Disconnect the transmission oil hoses (automatic)
Remove the radiator shroud and the radiator
Refit in the reverse order and fill the cooling system
Remove the alternator belt and the air pump belt
Remove the cooling fan
Check the pump for cracks, bearing noise, coolant leaks or other visible damage
how: Any of them: the pump is repaired or replaced.

do: Fit a dial indicator to the alternator bracket with its tip on the water pump pulley
Move the pulley up and down by hand and read the play
caution: Do not turn the pulley: the reading goes false.

do: Remove the air cleaner and disconnect the water temperature switch connector
Slip off the A/C compressor and power steering belts if fitted
Remove the air pump and the alternator, slipping off their belts
Remove the cooling fan and fan drive assembly and the A/C compressor pulley
Disconnect the radiator lower hose to drain the system and the upper hose
Remove the water pump
Bolt adapter 49 1975 145 to the pulley boss, support it on the press and press the shaft slowly out of the boss
Remove the snap ring, then support the pump body and press the shaft and bearing out through the front
Remove the impeller and tap the seal out with a piece of pipe

do: Press the new seal in straight with a piece of pipe and coat its lip with coolant

do: Press in the shaft and bearing with a piece of pipe and fit the snap ring
expect: The shaft turns smoothly.

do: Press on the impeller and the pulley boss
Fit the gasket and the shims, then the pump, and tighten evenly in order
Connect both radiator hoses and refit the pulleys, the fan and fan drive, the alternator and the air pump with their belts
Set the tension of each belt
how: Alternator SP-025; air pump SP-761; A/C SP-1001.

do: Reconnect the water temperature switch, refit the air cleaner and fill the cooling system
Start the engine, bleed the air from the coolant passages and top up

do: Warm the engine and let it idle
Connect a tachometer
Set the idle speed with the throttle adjust screw

do: Drop the engine quickly from 4000 rpm

do: Reconnect the vacuum sensing tube to the pipe
Stop the engine, reconnect the No.2 water temperature switch, remove the jumper and reconnect the No.1 switch
Start the engine and let it idle; on an automatic, disconnect the brown connector

do: Reconnect the hose; on an automatic, reconnect the brown connector

do: Disconnect the hose (purge valve to oil filler pipe) at the purge valve, put a finger over the valve's port and raise the engine to 2000 rpm
expect: Air is sucked into the port.

do: Reconnect the hose, stop the engine and remove the tachometer
Warm the engine to normal operating temperature
Inspect the hoses and connections for leaks
Listen to the air pump
expect: No excessive noise; replace the pump if there is.

do: Check the air pump drive belt tension and adjust it if needed
Disconnect the air hose (air pump to air control valve) at the air control valve
Connect the air pump gauge set to the hose and clamp the hose to the gauge
Connect a tachometer, start the engine and let it idle
Read the pressure on the gauge
expect: More than 11.5 kPa at 800 rpm; if not, replace the pump and test again.

do: Remove the air cleaner
Disconnect the air inlet and outlet hoses
Remove the air pump strap bolt, then the mounting bolt
Slip the drive belt off and lift the pump out
Fit the pump in the reverse order and set the belt tension
Check the belt for cracks, stretch, deterioration and oil or grease; replace it if needed
If the belt is noisy, check for looseness and misaligned pulleys

Move the pump toward or away from the engine until the tension is right
expect: 11 to 13 mm when pressed at 10 kg.

do: Tighten the mounting and strap bolts
To replace, loosen the air conditioner and power steering belts (if fitted) until the air pump belt can come off
Loosen the strap and mounting bolts and move the pump until the belt comes off
Fit the new belt and set its tension
Refit the air conditioner and power steering belts and set their tension
expect: 10 to 12 mm when pressed at 10 kg.

do: Intake manifold valve: disconnect the air hose (air pump to air control valve) at the air control valve
Connect a tachometer, start the engine and disconnect the switching solenoid valve connector
Raise the engine to 1500 rpm and watch the air inlet fitting on the air control valve
expect: No exhaust gas leaks out; if it does, replace the check valve.

do: To replace it, remove the air control valve, then the gasket and the check valve, and refit in the reverse order
how: The air control valve comes off as in PR-051.

do: Converter valve: disconnect the air hose (intake manifold to catalytic converter) at the rear of the intake manifold
Connect a tachometer, start the engine, raise it to 1500 rpm on the throttle and hold a finger at the air pipe opening
expect: No exhaust gas leaks back; if it does, replace the check valve.

do: To replace it, unclip and disconnect the air hose from the check valve
Loosen the split air pipe bolts and remove the air pipe assembly
Fit the new check valve and pipe assembly in the reverse order
Look over the pre-monolith and main monolith converters for cracks or damage
Check their connections are tight
Start the engine, let it idle and check the converter connections for exhaust leaks
To replace, remove the lower covers from the pre-monolith converter, the rear of the exhaust pipe and the main converter
Remove the catalyst thermo sensor
Remove the split air pipe from the main converter
Remove the converter brackets
Loosen the nuts joining the main converter's front flange to the No.2 pre-monolith converter
Support the converters
caution: Unsupported, they drop.

do: Loosen the nuts joining the rear of the exhaust pipe to the silencer
Remove the air pipe from the pre-monolith converter
Lower the exhaust pipe and main converter assembly from the car
Remove the pre-monolith converters by their nuts
Fit the converters in the reverse order
Warm the engine and connect a tachometer
Disconnect the air hose (air cleaner to air control valve) at the air cleaner and put a finger over it
Raise the engine speed
expect: Air flows out from 1500 to 2500 rpm up.

do: Let the engine idle and disconnect the vacuum sensing tube (relief solenoid valve to pipe) at the pipe
expect: Air flows out of the air hose.

do: Reconnect the tube and the air hose
Disconnect the split air hose (check valve to intake manifold) at the intake manifold and put a finger over the port
Disconnect the vacuum sensing tube (switching solenoid valve to pipe) at the pipe
expect: Air flows out of the port.

do: Reconnect the tube and the split air hose; replace the air control valve if it failed a check

Disconnect the port air solenoid connector
Remove the air control valve and fit the new one in the reverse order
Warm the engine, let it idle and connect a tachometer
Disconnect the throttle sensor connector and jumper terminals A and C of the connector
Disconnect the vacuum sensing tube (switching solenoid valve to pipe) at the pipe and put a finger over the tube
expect: Air is sucked into the tube at idle.

do: Raise the engine speed slowly
expect: No air is sucked in from 1000 to 1200 rpm up.

do: Disconnect the No.1 water temperature switch connector and jumper both its terminals
Pull the choke knob out about 15 mm (0.6 in) and raise the engine speed
expect: Air is sucked in at any speed.

do: Remove the jumper and reconnect the water temperature switch
Remove the jumper from the throttle sensor connector and reconnect the throttle sensor
Raise the engine speed slowly
expect: Air is sucked in at any speed (not when the engine is accelerated quickly).

do: Reconnect the vacuum sensing tube

expect: Air comes out of port C.

do: Disconnect the valve's connector, put battery power on its terminals and blow into tube B again
expect: Air comes out of port A.

do: Warm the engine, let it idle and connect a tachometer
Disconnect the throttle sensor connector and jumper terminals A and C of the connector
Disconnect the vacuum sensing tube (relief solenoid valve to pipe) at the pipe and put a finger over the tube
expect: Air is sucked into the tube at idle.

do: Raise the engine speed
expect: No air is sucked in from 3600 to 4400 rpm up.

do: Disconnect the catalyst thermo sensor connector and raise the engine speed slowly
expect: No air is sucked in from 1000 to 1200 rpm up.

do: Reconnect the catalyst thermo sensor
Remove the jumper from the throttle sensor connector and reconnect the throttle sensor

expect: No air is sucked in at any engine speed.

do: Remove the jumper and reconnect the heat hazard sensor
Stop the engine and disconnect the No.2 water temperature switch connector on the radiator
Disconnect the No.1 water temperature switch connector and jumper both its terminals
Pull the choke knob out about 15 mm (0.6 in), start the engine and raise the speed slowly
expect: No air is sucked in from 1000 to 1200 rpm up.

do: Reconnect the vacuum sensing tube to the pipe
Stop the engine, reconnect the No.2 water temperature switch, remove the jumper and reconnect the No.1 switch
Valve: disconnect the vacuum sensing tubes from the solenoid valve and the vacuum pipe and blow into the valve through tube B
expect: Air comes out of port C.

do: Disconnect the valve's connector, put battery power on its terminals and blow into tube B again
expect: Air comes out of port A.

do: Warm the engine, let it idle and connect a tachometer
Disconnect the throttle sensor connector and jumper terminals A and C of the connector
Put a voltmeter between the port air solenoid (GB) terminal and ground, raise the engine speed and read it
expect: Below 2 V to 3000 rpm, about 12 V from 3000 to 4000, below 2 V above 4000.

do: Remove the jumper and reconnect the throttle sensor
Put the car on a rolling road
caution: Secure the car with wire rope so it cannot move forward.

do: Raise the road speed and read the voltmeter
expect: Below 2 V under 50 mph, about 12 V above.

do: To replace, disconnect the valve's connector, remove the valve and fit the new one in the reverse order
Warm the engine, let it idle and connect a tachometer
Disconnect the throttle sensor connector and jumper terminals A and C of the connector
Put a voltmeter between the port air switching valve (R) terminal and ground, raise the engine speed and read it
expect: About 12 V to 3000 rpm, below 2 V from 3000 to 4000, about 12 V above 4000.

do: Remove the jumper and reconnect the throttle sensor
Put the car on a rolling road
caution: Secure the car with wire rope so it cannot move forward.

do: Raise the road speed and read the voltmeter
expect: About 12 V under 50 mph, below 2 V above.

do: To replace, disconnect the valve's connector, remove the valve and fit the new one in the reverse order
Disconnect the catalyst thermo sensor connector
Put an ohmmeter across the sensor's terminals
expect: Continuity; if none, replace the sensor.

do: To replace, loosen the sensor's mounting nuts, remove it and fit the new one in the reverse order
Turn the ignition on
expect: The heat hazard warning light comes on.

do: Start the engine
expect: The warning light goes off.

do: Disconnect the heat hazard sensor connector and jumper both its terminals
expect: The warning light comes on.

do: Sensor: remove the floor mat, disconnect the sensor's connector, undo its screws and remove it
Wrap the sensor and a thermometer in aluminium foil to keep the oil out and put them in oil
Connect a test lamp and battery across the sensor's terminals
how: The figure shows the hook-up; it was not read.

do: Heat the oil slowly
expect: The lamp lights when the foil reaches 130 +/- 10 C; if not, replace the sensor.
caution: Never heat the oil above 150 C.

do: Refit the sensor in the reverse order
Remove the No.1 switch from the water pump and the No.2 switch from the radiator lower tank
Put the switch in water with a thermometer and heat the water slowly
No.1 switch: note the temperature at which continuity between its terminals stops
expect: No continuity above 70 +/- 6.5 C.

do: No.2 switch: note the temperature at which continuity begins
expect: Continuity above 15 +/- 3 C.

do: Disconnect the choke switch connector
Check continuity between the numbered terminals with the knob in and pulled out
Disconnect the choke relay connector
Check continuity between the relay's numbered terminals without power, then with battery power
Warm the engine, let it idle and connect a tachometer
Disconnect the throttle sensor connector and jumper terminals A and C of the connector
Put a voltmeter between the main air bleed control solenoid (Br) terminal and ground, raise the engine speed and read it
expect: About 12 V to 3000 rpm, below 2 V from 3000 to 4000, about 12 V above 4000.

do: Remove the jumper and reconnect the throttle sensor
Put the car on a rolling road
caution: Secure the car with wire rope so it cannot move forward.

do: Raise the road speed and read the voltmeter
expect: About 12 V under 50 mph, below 2 V above.

do: Warm the engine, let it idle and connect a tachometer; on an automatic, disconnect the brown connector
how: The figure shows which connector; it was not read.

do: Disconnect the air hose (coasting valve to air cleaner) at the air cleaner and put a finger over it
expect: No air is sucked in at idle.

do: Take the engine above 3000 rpm and drop it quickly
expect: Air is sucked into the hose until the speed falls to 1000 to 1200 rpm.

do: Valve: disconnect the vacuum sensing tubes from the solenoid valve and the vacuum pipe and blow into the valve through tube B
expect: Air comes out of port C.

do: Disconnect the valve's connector, put battery power on its terminals and blow into tube B again
expect: Air comes out of the air filter A.

do: Coasting valve: remove the air cleaner and the carburettor
Disconnect the air hose and the vacuum sensing tube from the coasting valve
Loosen its mounting bolts, remove it and fit the new one in the reverse order
Warm the engine and let it idle
No.1: disconnect the air hose (air control valve to air pump) at the air pump and put a finger over it
expect: No air is sucked in at idle.

do: Take the engine above 3000 rpm and drop it quickly
expect: Air is sucked in for a few seconds while decelerating; if not, replace the air control valve.

do: No.2: disconnect the air hose (air cleaner to No.2 anti-afterburn valve) at the air cleaner and put a finger over it
expect: No air is sucked in at idle.

do: Take the engine above 3000 rpm and drop it quickly
expect: Air is sucked in for a few seconds while decelerating; if not, replace the No.2 anti-afterburn valve.

do: Remove the air cleaner
Check the dash pot rod does not keep the throttle lever off the idle stop
Open the throttle lever fully and quickly
expect: The dash pot rod extends quickly.

do: Release the throttle lever
expect: It returns slowly to idle after touching the rod.

do: Connect a tachometer, start and warm the engine and confirm the idle speed
Move the throttle lever off the dash pot rod, then lower the engine speed slowly and note the speed at which the lever just touches the rod
If it is out, loosen the lock nut and turn the dash pot diaphragm
Warm the engine and connect a tachometer
Disconnect the vacuum sensing tube (leading vacuum advance diaphragm to pipe) at the pipe and put a finger over the pipe
expect: No air is sucked in at idle.

do: Raise the engine speed slowly
expect: Air is sucked into the pipe from 1000 to 1200 rpm up.

do: Drop the engine quickly from 4000 rpm
expect: No air is sucked in while decelerating.

do: Automatic: let the engine idle with a drive range selected
how: SP-1584. The page names the lever positions; the OCR text lost two of them.
expect: Air is sucked into the pipe.

do: Disconnect the No.1 water temperature switch connector and jumper both its terminals
Pull the choke knob out about 15 mm (0.6 in)
expect: No air is sucked in at any engine speed.

do: Stop the engine and disconnect the No.2 water temperature switch connector on the radiator
Pull the choke knob out about 15 mm (0.6 in), start the engine and raise the speed
expect: Air is sucked in from 1000 to 1200 rpm up.

do: Trailing: repeat every step on the tube from the trailing vacuum advance diaphragm
expect: Air is sucked in from 2900 to 3100 rpm up; none at idle or while decelerating from 4000 rpm.

do: Each valve: disconnect the vacuum sensing tubes from the solenoid valve and the vacuum pipe and blow into the valve through tube B
expect: Air comes out of the air filter C.

do: Disconnect the valve's connector, put battery power on its terminals and blow into tube B again
expect: Air comes out of port A.

do: Disconnect the ventilation hose from the canister and connect the U-tube gauge to it
Feed in low-pressure air slowly until the water levels differ by the test figure
expect: 356 +/- 12 mm of water.

do: Blank off the U-tube's inlet and leave it five minutes
expect: The level stays within the band the page's figure shows; the figure was not read.

do: If it drops further, look for a leaking or loose evaporative line, a leaking fuel tank, a leaking or loose fuel line or a leaking filler cap
Remove the check and cut valve
Connect a pressure gauge to the fuel tank passage and blow through the valve
how: SP-1085. Hold the valve horizontal: tilted, its own weight closes the passage.
expect: It opens at 5.5 to 7 kPa.

do: Move the gauge to the atmosphere passage and blow through the valve
expect: It opens at 1 to 5 kPa.

do: To replace, raise the rear of the car and support it on stands
Undo the hose bands, disconnect the evaporative hoses and remove the valve
Fit the valve in the reverse order
how: Note which hose goes where and which way the valve's fittings face; push the hoses fully on and band them.

do: Look the canister over for leaking carbon and tap it with a finger
expect: No carbon leaks and no abnormal sound.

do: Disconnect the hose (purge valve to oil filler pipe) at the purge valve, start the engine, let it idle and put a finger on the port
expect: No air is drawn in at idle.

do: Raise the engine to 2000 rpm
expect: Air is drawn into the port.

do: Check the air vent hose for cracks or damage and disconnect it from the ventilation pipe
Blow slowly through the hose with the ignition off
expect: Air passes through the air vent solenoid valve.

do: Turn the ignition on and blow again
expect: No air passes.

do: Confirm the fuel filter was changed within its interval
Remove the air cleaner assembly and disconnect the fuel main hose at the carburettor
caution: Spilled fuel can ignite.

do: Connect a pressure gauge, a restrictor and hoses so the fuel discharges into a graduated container
Disconnect the fuel pump cut relay connector and fit a jumper wire
how: The figure shows the terminals; it was not read.

do: Turn the ignition on and open the restrictor for a moment to vent the system into the container
Close the restrictor, let the pressure settle and read it
expect: 20 to 25 kPa.

do: With the pressure in range, open the restrictor, time the fuel into the container, then close it
expect: 1400 cc or more within one minute.

do: Remove the storage compartment behind the driver's seat and disconnect the fuel pump connector
Raise the rear of the car and support it on stands
Remove the fuel pump protector cover
Disconnect the inlet and outlet hoses and remove the pump
Fit the new pump in the reverse order
how: Push the hoses fully onto the pump's fittings and clip them.

do: Raise the rear of the car and support it on stands
Loosen the clips at both ends of the filter and disconnect the fuel hoses
Remove the filter from its retainer
Fit the new filter and connect the hoses
how: Push the hoses fully onto the filter and clip them.

do: Drain the fuel from the tank
caution: Keep sparks, cigarettes and open flames away from the tank.

do: Raise the rear of the car and support it on stands
Remove the tank protectors
Disconnect the fuel main hose, the return hose and the evaporation hoses from the tank
Remove the fixing band bolts and lower the tank
Check the tank for cracks and corrosion; repair or replace it
caution: Before any repair, steam-clean the tank until all explosive gas is gone.

do: Refit in the reverse order, pushing the main, return and evaporation hoses onto the tank fittings
expect: Fittings more than 25 mm into the hoses.

do: Push the filler hose onto the tank pipe and the filler pipe
expect: More than 40 mm on each.

do: Check the fuel cut valve for cracks or damage
To replace it, disconnect its hoses, undo its bolts, remove it and fit the new one in the reverse order
how: Push the hoses fully on and clip them; follow the arrow marks on the valve body.

do: Check the fuel check valve for cracks or damage; to replace it, pull it out of its hoses and fit the new one
how: SP-1066. Push the valve fully into the hose ends and clip it; the arrow points as the page's figure shows, which was not read.

do: Inspect the fuel lines for leaks and tighten their connections
If much dirt or water is found, drain the tank and blow the lines out with compressed air
When replacing a fuel hose, push it onto its pipe
expect: Pipe 30 to 35 mm into the hose.

do: Move the intake air temperature control valve inside the air cleaner by hand
expect: It moves freely and its spring pushes back.

do: Idle compensator, bimetal cold: suck on its tube
expect: The valve is closed; replace the compensator if it leaks much.

do: Idle compensator, bimetal above about 69 C: check the valve
expect: The valve is open; if not, replace the compensator.

do: Altitude compensator: remove the air cleaner and start the engine
expect: It runs smoothly.

do: Cover the slow port on the carburettor air horn with a finger
expect: Above 500 to 1500 m of altitude the idle speed drops.

do: If it does not, remove the altitude compensator valve and blow through it between ports A and B
how: SP-1072. The opening point moves with atmospheric pressure.
expect: Air passes above 500 to 1500 m of altitude.

do: Remove the air cleaner and press the accelerator pedal to the floor
expect: The carburettor's throttle valves stand vertical, wide open.

do: Check the linkage returns fully without binding and the choke control moves freely
Check the pedal height against the brake pedal; set it with nut A
expect: 42 +/- 5 mm lower than the brake pedal.

do: Check the cable's free play at the carburettor; set it with nut B
expect: 1 to 3 mm.

do: Press the pedal to the floor and check the throttle valves are wide open; set with stopper bolt C
Remove the air cleaner cover, disconnect the idle compensator tube, the air pump inlet hose, the hot air hose and the air hoses, and remove the air cleaner
how: The page lists items 1 to 24 in removal order against a figure.

do: Remove the No.2 anti-afterburn valve and bracket assembly
Disconnect the choke heater lead connector, the throttle sensor connector and the main air bleed control solenoid valve
Disconnect the metering oil pump connecting rod, and on a manual car the richer solenoid valve connector
Disconnect the hot start assist cable, the accelerator cable, the throttle opener's vacuum sensing tube, the cruise control cable and the choke cable
Disconnect the air vent hose, the sub-zero start assist fluid hose (not California), the fuel return hose and the fuel main hose
Disconnect the metering oil pump tubes and the air vent solenoid valve connector
Undo the carburettor attaching nuts and lift the carburettor off
Refit in the reverse order, pushing the fuel main and return hoses onto the carburettor's fittings
expect: Fittings 30 to 35 mm into the hoses.

do: Start the engine and check for fuel leaks and the fuel level
expect: Fuel at the mark in the sight glass.

do: Check the accelerator pump: car level, air cleaner cover off, engine run until the fuel is at the mark, then stopped; work the throttle
expect: Fuel squirts from the pump nozzles.

do: Set the idle speed and the idle mixture
how: PR-016 for the speed, PR-078 for the mixture.

do: Air horn: disconnect the vacuum sensing tubes for the altitude compensator valve, the choke delay valve and the No.2 choke diaphragm and the choke heater lead; remove the altitude compensator valve
how: The page lists items 1 to 23 in removal order against a figure.

do: Remove the throttle opener and bracket, the No.1 choke diaphragm's tube, the dash pot and bracket, the throttle return spring, the sub-return spring and their bracket
Remove the bimetal spring housing and bracket assembly, the fast idle rod, the hot start assist lever spring and the bracket
Remove the No.2 choke diaphragm, the air horn attaching screws and the air horn assembly
From the air horn, remove the float pin, float, needle valve and hook spring, spring and valve stem
Main body: free the accelerator pump rod and the secondary throttle valve rod (split pins), remove the throttle sensor, undo the main body attaching bolts and lift the main body off
From the main body, remove the diaphragm cover, return spring, clip, diaphragm, housing and lever and gasket, then the accelerator pump lever, its cover, diaphragm and return spring
how: Items 1 to 12 are partly lost in the OCR text and the figure was not read.

do: Remove the pump nozzle screw, nozzle and gasket, the weights, the outlet and inlet check valves and the check valve seat
Remove the retainer, blind plug and washer, then the primary and secondary main jets

Remove the secondary No.2 step air bleed, secondary step jet, secondary and primary main air bleeds, primary slow jet, primary No.2 slow air bleed and air bleed, and on a manual car the richer air bleed, jet and blind plug
Throttle body: saw off the idle limiter cap and remove the mixture adjust screw inside it
how: The figure shows the cut; it was not read.

do: Wash every part in clean solvent and blow the fuel passages out with compressed air
caution: Never clean a jet with wire.

do: Inspect the air horn, main body and throttle body for cracks, the choke and throttle shafts for wear, the linkage and rods for bends, the return springs, every jet and air bleed for clogging and the diaphragms for damage
Inspect the float for damage, the needle valve and seat for wear or rust and the strainer for clogging
Put battery power on the air vent solenoid valve, and on a manual car the richer solenoid valve
expect: The valve stem pulls into the valve body.

do: Assemble in the reverse order with new gaskets, every part clean and sound
how: Primary and secondary parts look alike; do not swap them.

do: Fit the new mixture adjust screw
expect: Seated lightly, then three turns out.

do: Before fitting the air horn, set the float level: air horn inverted and float hanging, measure float to air horn gasket (H); bend the float seat lip to set it
Turn the air horn upright, float hanging, and measure float bottom to gasket (L); bend the float stopper to set it
Fit the bimetal spring housing to the main body with the choke valve closed and the vacuum diaphragm shaft pulled, so the choke shaft lever sits on the bimetal spring
Fast idle: with the choke valve fully closed, measure primary throttle valve to bore wall; bend the fast idle rod to set it
Choke valve opening: disconnect the tubes from the No.1 vacuum diaphragm, pull the choke lever link fully out and hold it, apply more than 500 mmHg and measure G1, then G2
No.2 choke diaphragm: disconnect its tube, pull the choke lever link fully out with the choke valve fully closed (cool the bimetal if needed), apply more than 500 mmHg and measure R
